# V71 · documentary refinement

Authorized scope: refine the existing source 00:00–04:55 sequence after Joshua's V70 coverage audit. His instruction “Then fix these” authorizes this pass. He prefers a more dramatic, story-driven treatment. The separate missing ending is not implemented here.

## Result

The native factory timeline previously ran approximately 08:17.939. A reversible, monotonic story clock now brings the existing material to approximately 04:56.600, including the already present short pose handoff. Eighty-nine authored landmark anchors align the existing scenes to the reference's approximate narrative placement. Native keyframes and renderer clocks remain intact; this is authored timing, not recovered camera or phoneme alignment. The original 1920×1080 reference decodes through PTS 320.805 seconds despite its filename.

Changes include an animated town callout, quieter opening fire/blur, a less extreme aerial move with aspect-preserving image cover, smaller anchored noir words, shorter blast/impact treatment, bounded cutout stance correction and foot shadows, projected foreground rubble, brighter projected cable emphasis, smaller role words below faces, softer eye-fire alpha and a restrained edge finish. Globe V70 drama and V68 animated shoe dashes remain intact. Existing scenes, visual assets and alternatives are retained.

## Controls and preservation

Open the editor → depot controls → Documentary refinement. Disable “Use V71 refinement” to restore the V70 profile and native timing. The original V70 source files are retained under `dist/assets/archive/v70-refinement/`. A first-use settings/effects snapshot is recorded as `beforeRefinementV71` in local settings.

“Preserve custom artwork/framing values” applies the new visual defaults only where the old factory values remain, or a value was missing. Custom scene durations and keyframes remain stored; narration-timing mode intentionally remaps their playback to story landmarks. Disable narration timing to use native durations. Timeline playhead position survives initialization and mode switches. Map label, stance/shadow/rubble/cable amounts, eye mask and vignette are editable. The town focus is an illustrative ellipse, not a surveyed municipal boundary.

Attach narration/soundtrack accepts a user-owned audio/video track. Enable its playback checkbox and press Play. It follows story seconds, seeks and pauses; replacements archive prior local tracks in a separate database. No reference narration or voice clone is bundled. The V70 globe sound system remains separate.

## Evidence and limits

- 33 late-sequence stills per version, plus 15 early stills per version, rendered through production scene APIs on CPU Canvas. The before side uses V70 parameters and disabled refinement at the same native pose. Early software city/chess renders cannot certify GPU reflection or depth appearance. Battle SVG decoding remains subject to the prior offline harness limitation.
- A silent 24 fps, 19.33-second comparison covers walking, cable focus, sales typography, rival heads and manufacturing typography. It is a selected-scenes review, not a complete five-minute export. Each comparison side uses the same native scene pose and the V71 story clock, so it isolates visual changes rather than demonstrating V70's longer pacing.
- Sampled source frames retained with exact requested timestamps. Reference timestamps, source-to-native knots and original asset hashes are machine-readable.
- 29,660 monotonic/inverse timing samples, 89 exact anchors; initialization/playhead preservation; disabled profile and custom-value preservation; native clock/state restoration even after render errors; attached audio seek/pause/rate; six walking cycles and bounded stance reset checks; animation library insertion/default/hash checks; relevant scene and asset checks passed.
- An old model-expansion regression expected the pre-V65 history endpoint. It was corrected to assert the retained shoe segment endpoint and the existing chapter tail separately; no production endpoint was shortened to satisfy it.
- All 247 original asset files match V70 byte-for-byte. No new generated bitmap or third-party asset is necessary for this procedural refinement.

Walking remains an image-space photographic puppet with bounded stance correction, not a full world-space no-slip or motion-capture solution. Town/city imagery remains illustrative. Full continuous native-browser playback, UI performance, device audio latency and a complete five-minute final render remain unverified. User visual acceptance is pending. No deployment or repository push occurred.

The original ending after roughly 04:55 still needs its separate reconstruction: complete pose/question marks, interior/boot/football, second lineup and library beats. This pass does not claim that coverage.
